claims.text: Typical functional constipation: no tests unless usual treatment fails.
claims.quote: For patients whose histories are consistent with functional constipation, no tests are needed unless there is no response to conventional treatment of constipation.

claims.text: Abdominal X-ray if treatment fails or an organic cause is suspected.
claims.quote: An abdominal radiograph should be done if patients have been unresponsive to treatment or an organic cause is suspected.

claims.text: Hirschsprung disease: barium enema, rectal manometry and rectal biopsy.
claims.quote: Barium enema, rectal manometry, and biopsy (Hirschsprung disease)

claims.text: Tethered cord or spinal tumor: lumbosacral spine X-rays, with MRI considered.
claims.quote: Plain radiographs of lumbosacral spine; MRI considered (tethered spinal cord or tumor)

claims.text: Blood lead level for lead poisoning.
Infant botulism: stool for botulinum toxin.
Cystic fibrosis: sweat test and genetic testing.
claims.quote: Sweat test and genetic testing (cystic fibrosis)

claims.text: Metabolic causes: calcium and other electrolytes.
Celiac disease: serology, usually IgA tissue transglutaminase antibodies.
claims.quote: Serologic screening usually for IgA antibodies to tissue transglutaminase (celiac disease)
